```

### Frozen-rollout baseline ablation (27 October 2026)

The existing four-duel PPO rollout freezes policy weights but, in its default
`online` mode, updates the moving return baseline after each duel. An opt-in
`--ppo-baseline-timing frozen_rollout` uses the pre-rollout baseline for all
four advantage calculations. The learner and opponent still receive only their own
player-visible observations. Tests cover both timings and confirm identical
native results across serial, process-worker, and batched-inference rollouts.

The original frozen-rollout run below used a flawed moving-baseline update:
each game replaced the estimate using the same frozen pre-rollout value, so
only the last game's reward affected the estimate carried to the next rollout.
The implementation now accumulates every terminal reward while retaining the
frozen pre-rollout value for that rollout's advantages. The checkpoint and
measurements below remain reproducible historical results of the old update
rule; they are not evidence for the corrected update rule's strength.

Starting from the same unchanged feature-v23 reference and using the same
32-game post-patch PPO schedule and settings as the online run above, the
frozen-baseline child completed **32/32** terminal duels, with **5,542 learner
decisions** and measured training wall time **38.09 s** with one Torch thread.
All 32 saved trajectories replay-verified and passed the visibility audit;
the audit shortlisted 69 review candidates. The ignored checkpoint is
`.cache/goat-ai/fv23_patched_core_ppo_frozen_baseline_21200_21231.pt`, SHA-256
`504c32544be81daf831c26b8aeee41685000b986abf5b49cbfe257b7065a41f0`.
Its replay-audit report SHA-256 is
`17d23e974377a702296436f5a8fe7158c06b037e9387daa2615d94cd1e138b9f`.

On held-out Phoenix Control versus two separately sourced Dimension Fusion
decks, with both deck assignments and policy seats, seeds 21500–21507 gave
the frozen child **28–36** directly against the online-baseline PPO child over
64 games. Its score interval was **34.4%–51.6%**. A separate direct comparison
on seeds 21516–21523 gave the frozen child **31–33** against the unchanged
parent, with score interval **40.6%–56.2%**. On a matched Tactical-v14 schedule
at seeds 21508–21515, the frozen child scored **13–51**, the online child
**10–54**, and the unchanged parent **10–54** over 64 games each. The frozen
minus parent paired score difference was **+4.7 percentage points**, 95%
interval **−1.6 to +10.9 points**. Local-deck and native-asset report
comparisons passed for both Tactical deck pairs. The ignored reports are
`.cache/goat-ai/frozen_vs_online_ppo_phoenix_*.json`,
`.cache/goat-ai/frozen_ppo_vs_parent_phoenix_*.json`, and the matched
`*_ppo_vs_tactical_phoenix_*.json` files. All evaluations used
`--engine experimental --both-deck-assignments --require-unseen-main-decks
--max-decisions 3000`. The new timing has no established strength gain, and
neither PPO child is promoted.

### Leave-one-out PPO rollout baseline (27 October 2026)

An opt-in `--ppo-baseline-timing leave_one_out` now centers each completed
duel's terminal reward against the *other* games in the same frozen-policy
rollout and learner-deck group. Its baseline cannot depend on that duel's
sampled actions or outcome. A singleton group uses the pre-rollout moving
estimate. Games with no learner policy choice still contribute their outcome
to other games' baselines. The moving estimates continue to accumulate every
terminal result for later singleton fallbacks. This changes training updates,
not agent-visible observations or the simulator. Unit tests cover paired
rewards, separate deck groups, empty learner records, and a final singleton;
native tests confirm serial, process-worker, and batched-inference modes
produce equal trajectories, reports, and model tensors.

A matched four-role, 32-game ablation used the same selected parent, training
decks, seeds 46000–46031, four workers, four-game PPO rollouts, per-episode
weighting, learner-deck scope, three epochs, batch size 16, learning rate
0.0001, and parent KL weight 0.5 as the corrected frozen-baseline check above.
Only `--ppo-baseline-timing leave_one_out` changed. All 32 games terminated:
17 learner wins, 15 losses, 4,064 learner decisions, 23,487 total decisions,
and measured training wall time 25.36 s with one Torch thread. All 32 saved
trajectories independently replay-verified and passed the visibility audit;
38 possible mistakes were shortlisted. The ignored checkpoint is
`.cache/goat-ai/fv23_loo_ppo_46000_46031.pt` (SHA-256
`054c40ee0a1d85cebbc7a53026c833f6bbbfd816f6db990dfb5b226147a82de0`),
and the ignored audit is
`.cache/goat-ai/fv23_loo_ppo_46000_46031_audit.json` (SHA-256
`52516cb28265fb377af51cb15c4ed96b5f429cb5922ad43a932fbd8d29719127`).

On unseen Rhymus Goat Control versus Charlotte Zombie, both deck assignments
and seats, seeds 46100–46107, the child scored **16–15–1** directly against
the matched frozen-baseline child (paired-bootstrap 95% score interval
39.1–64.1%) and **17–15** against the selected parent (31.3–68.8%). Against
Tactical v14, the leave-one-out and frozen-baseline children each scored
**15–17**, while the parent scored **16–16**. The verified paired child-minus-

The report comparator checked matched native/source fingerprints, current
local deck hashes, and absence of evaluation Main Deck compositions from

`d96dbd7f3b8a84df6c80a1e7c4ec774140a748eba6510e3e5ff78b0de57d1352`
(direct versus frozen), `1a25ad64cd0de083880cf458fe01257df18d529899224c52e89091a3605e144a`

`f5814f252a5e72d6bec3fa17459fdbb6d28622c15f2734d658227a1a84bbd5e9`

### Visible-rule v2 preference ablation (27 October 2026)

The `visible_audit_v2` automated-label experiment adds two narrow categories
to v1: activating Nobleman of Crossout while only one's own set monsters are
visible, and choosing one's own card for Raigeki Break when a legal opposing
field target exists. For the first category the alternative is an offered
Battle Phase transition from Main Phase 1 (or End Phase from Main Phase 2);
for the second it is an offered opposing field target. These are synthetic
pairwise hypotheses, not human-reviewed optimal-play labels. The v1 rule set
remains unchanged and old v1 label files continue to validate against v1.

The old 21200–21231 replays failed current-asset verification because they
recorded the pre-correction Dark Balter script. A fresh 32-duel frozen-policy
rollout from the unchanged feature-v23 reference used control/Chaos probe
decks, seeds 24000–24031, one PPO rollout with four workers, and the current
experimental native core. All duels terminated after **24,509 decisions**,
including **4,034 learner decisions**. Full native replay verification and
visibility auditing of these source games produced **12 preferences from
eight replays**: four Chaos Sorcerer self-banish, four new Nobleman cases,
three weak Flip summons, and one BLS self-banish. No Raigeki Break case was
present in this sample. The label manifest SHA-256 is
`8bfbcc86ab6acc212cab5a1fe0a998e7fabdd3234426096a308f15881c9a3d39`.

A parent-KL fit used those 12 labels, 64 distinct current-asset preservation
states from seeds 23000–23003, 100 steps, learning rate 0.0001, and KL weight
1.0. Preference loss fell from 1.8301 to 0.2247; final preservation KL was
0.0454. The ignored child checkpoint
`.cache/goat-ai/fv23_visible_rule_v2_24000_24031.pt` has SHA-256
`ac23fd824a439769e0c1945aa36e404514abf56f64afa1018259e72cd01336a3`.
Learning those comparisons is not a competitive-strength result.

On unseen Phoenix Control versus the GoatFormat and WikiFormat Dimension

its paired-bootstrap score interval was **45.3%–62.5%**. On matched seeds
25008–25015 against Tactical-v14, the child scored **13–49–2** and the
parent **18–46** over 64 duels each. The report comparator checked identical

### Visible resource v3 counterfactual preference experiment (27 October 2026)

The saved-report comparator now has `--require-unseen-main-decks` for M4
comparisons. It verifies both local YDK files against their report hashes,
recomputes each Main Deck composition hash, and rejects a composition present
in either checkpoint's recorded training games. It fails closed for older
reports without composition provenance. On the existing 64-game Zombie
child/parent Tactical reports below, the gate passed and reproduced the
paired +14.06-point difference (95% interval +3.125 to +23.4375 points).
This verifies the exact Main Deck multisets, not archetype independence.

  --require-unseen-main-decks
```

The source was 64 current-core PPO self-play replays on seeds 34000–34063.
`scripts/derive_visible_rule_preferences.py --rule-set visible_resource_v3`
replay-verified and visibility-audited every duel before emitting **137
synthetic preferences from 25 replays**. Of these, 128 compared a recorded
safe choice with an offered resource loss; nine compared a recorded loss with
an offered phase transition. There were 44 Nobleman and 100 Heavy Storm
category occurrences; a decision can carry both categories. Repeated
near-identical resource contexts in one replay were deduplicated, though one
replay still contributed 38 preferences. The ignored manifest is
`.cache/goat-ai/visible_resource_v3_dedup_34000_34063/manifest.json`
(SHA-256 `ff7a0f0ddf8a025cd781219c2e55467294922b3864e216fde137ff35ffdb241c`).

used all 137 preferences plus 64 preservation states from four
parent-provenance Tactical replays on seeds 33016–33019. The fit used
preservation batch 8, KL weight 1, learning rate 0.0001, and seed 57.
Preference loss went from **0.1893 to 0.0969**; final preservation KL was

### Exchanged Thunder Dragon native ruling fixture (27 October 2026)

The [period Thunder Dragon FAQ](https://www.goatformat.com/rulings7.html)
allows the controller of an opponent-owned copy obtained through Exchange to
discard it and search that controller's own Deck. The new seed-28 fixture
starts with Exchange in player 0's hand and two Thunder Dragons in player
1's hand. Exchange transfers one Dragon to player 0, who discards it and
selects two copies from their own Deck. Player 0's Deck falls from 34 to 32,
player 1's remains at 35, and the discarded card reaches player 1's
Graveyard. The opponent receives the two-card search reveal and remembers
both copies in the opponent-hand multiset. The scripted line is followed by
random legal play until terminal; the complete trajectory serializes,
replay-verifies, and passes the visibility audit. The focused Exchange and
Thunder Dragon native suite passed **5/5 tests**. This establishes the
specific pinned-core behavior, not every Exchange or banish-replacement
interaction.

Reproduce with pinned native assets:

```bash
GOAT_AI_NATIVE_ROOT=.cache/goat-ai PYTHONPATH=src:. .venv/bin/pytest -q \
  tests/test_historical_thunder_exchange.py \
  tests/test_historical_thunder_dragon.py \
  tests/test_historical_exchange.py
```

### Thunder Dragon under Banisher of the Light (27 October 2026)

The [period Thunder Dragon FAQ](https://www.goatformat.com/rulings7.html)
permits activating its effect even when Banisher of the Light redirects the
discard away from the Graveyard. A seed-3 native fixture Normal Summons
Banisher, discards GOAT Thunder Dragon, and selects two copies from its own
Deck. The discarded copy is face-up banished; none enters its controller's
Graveyard. Its Deck falls from 34 to 32, and only the opponent receives the
two-card search reveal and remembers both copies in hand. The scripted line
continues with random legal choices to a terminal result; the complete
trajectory serializes, replay-verifies, and passes the visibility audit.
The focused Thunder Dragon/Exchange native suite passed **5/5 tests**.
This validates the pinned engine's behavior for one replacement effect, not
all banishment or Exchange interactions.

GOAT_AI_NATIVE_ROOT=.cache/goat-ai PYTHONPATH=src:. .venv/bin/pytest -q \
  tests/test_historical_thunder_dragon.py \

The feature-v23 policy averages all visible state cards into one vector. An
opt-in v26 branch adds separate own/opponent visible-card means through a
zero-initialized residual projection. It uses the same v23 decision inputs,
preserves exact parent logits before training, and leaves hidden-card values
absent from the encoded inputs. A unit test checks exact warm-start logits,
batched-forward equivalence, and a strict parent-version gate.

Matched v23 control and v26 child continuations used the same feature-v23
parent, eight replay-verified fixed-policy games from seed 44000–44003,
437 Tactical-v14 labels on policy-visited states, one epoch, batch size 16,
seed 81, learning rate 0.0002, and identical optimizer settings. Their final
training losses were **0.6391** (v23) and **0.5974** (v26). This is a
training-set fit comparison, not a strength metric. The ignored checkpoints
are `.cache/goat-ai/v23_owner_pool_control_44000_44003.pt` (SHA-256
`852f5704062b65b85c35c0ba539456a12b45bacaba58e3293b97ad1b470e334c`)
and `.cache/goat-ai/v26_owner_pool_child_44000_44003.pt` (SHA-256
`38169149494acf547cc8009e688b357875ef4e39c95403db389677e463050a10`).

On Rhymus New Jersey versus Charlotte Zombie, both Main Deck assignments,
both policy seats, and held-out seeds 37200–37207, v26 scored **13–19**
directly against v23 over 32 terminal duels (paired-bootstrap 95% score
interval **31.25–46.875%**; maximum 873 decisions). It scored **4–12** as
first player and **9–7** as second. This does not justify promoting v26;
the tested continuation was weaker on this matchup. The ignored direct
report is `.cache/goat-ai/v26_owner_pool_vs_v23_rhymus_zombie_37200_37207.json`
(SHA-256 `c427082b577ab498b627e8e78cd7089c24f512947dbe6fe5dc60a8ce5c275a96`).

### Action-conditioned visible-card attention, feature v27 (27 October 2026)

The current feature-v23 policy uses one mean of visible cards for every legal
action. An opt-in v27 branch lets each action attend to the player-visible
cards before scoring it. The residual output starts at zero, so loading the
selected v23 checkpoint preserves its exact initial logits; a unit test also
checks mixed-length padded batches after the attention weights become nonzero.
The branch reads only `encode_decision` inputs, with unknown opponent cards
still represented by unknown identities. It does not inspect native hidden
state or change the default inference policy.

A matched continuation used the same eight replay-verified fixed-policy games
and **437** Tactical-v14 labels as the [v23/v26 control](#separate-player-card-pools-feature-v26-27-october-2026), with one epoch,
batch size 16, seed 81, and learning rate 0.0002. The v27 training loss was
**0.6069**, versus **0.6391** for the prior matched v23 control. This measures
fit on synthetic teacher decisions only. The ignored checkpoint is
`.cache/goat-ai/v27_attention_child_44000_44003.pt` (SHA-256
`03d4ebd9880210c0f73f1a5442011a7a655b92eb086b98885794e60dca24ebbe`).

**31.25–50%**). On held-out Phoenix 2005 Control/WikiFormat Dimension Fusion
under the same balanced schedule, it scored **19–13** (interval
**46.875–71.875%**). The two point scores sum to 32–32, and each family's
interval includes 50%; the result does not establish a robust improvement.
The four exact Main Deck compositions are absent from both checkpoints'

### Native worker scaling on sourced decks (27 October 2026)

Eight RandomAgent duels used Matt Peddle's sourced 2005 Goat Control Main Deck
against the sourced Riclar 2020 Chaos Turbo Main Deck, paired across seats on
seeds 49800–49803. The pinned experimental native adapter, identical decks and
assets, a 3,000-decision cap, and `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` were held fixed. Runs
were sequential on an Intel Core i7-10700K with 16 logical CPUs and 46 GiB of
RAM. Every game reached terminal; all three worker counts produced the same
winners and **8,150 total decisions**, including identical per-game decision
counts. Wall time includes process spawn and shutdown.

| Spawned workers | Wall time | Duels/s | Decisions/s | Mean reset/duel | Sum of worker peak RSS |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 2.691 s | 2.973 | 3,028 | 61.1 ms | 118,308 KiB |
| 4 | 1.518 s | 5.271 | 5,369 | 64.0 ms | 229,352 KiB |
| 8 | 1.125 s | 7.112 | 7,246 | 87.7 ms | 447,036 KiB |

The sums combine each worker's Linux `VmHWM`, so they are **not** simultaneous
machine-wide memory peaks. Parent peak RSS was 26,680, 26,568, and 26,388 KiB
respectively. These are single short runs, not confidence intervals for
throughput or a forecast for long training; they exclude neural inference,
trajectory writing, and verification. On this schedule eight workers were
2.39 times as fast as two, with 3.78 times the summed worker high-water
memory. Larger schedules and inference batching still need measurement.

Reproduce from the pinned native setup at commit `0d14fc1` with:

```bash

    --deck-a examples/decks/goat_control_matt_peddle_indianapolis_2005.ydk \
    --deck-b examples/decks/chaos_turbo_riclar_2020.ydk \
    --seed 49800 --games 8 --workers "$workers" \
    --output ".cache/goat-ai/parallel_2005_matt_chaos_49800_${workers}w.json"
done
```

The [native duel scaling pilot](#native-worker-scaling-on-sourced-decks-27-october-2026)

feature-v23 checkpoint, used one epoch, width 32, batch size 16, batched
forward, omitted forced forwards, learning rate 0.0002, seed 58, and one

reduce simple order bias. Source replays and their labels were unchanged.

| Run | Verification workers | External wall time | CLI verification time | CLI fitting time |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4 | 7.031 s | 2.552 s | 1.775 s |
| 2 | 8 | 7.143 s | 2.791 s | 1.591 s |
| 3 | 8 | 7.047 s | 2.724 s | 1.572 s |
| 4 | 4 | 6.913 s | 2.611 s | 1.571 s |

The two 4-worker runs averaged **6.972 s** externally; the 8-worker runs
averaged **7.095 s**. Verification itself averaged 2.582 versus 2.758 s.

law. All four checkpoints recorded the same `0.14908188252774301` epoch
loss, identical source hashes, and byte-equal values for all 38 model-state

the measured choice for this eight-replay job; a larger corpus might have
a different optimum. This check does not measure playing strength.

### Strict Heavy Storm card-advantage ablation (27 October 2026)

The existing opt-in `tactical_card_advantage` variant filters Heavy Storm when
its visible opposing backrow count does not exceed the friendly cards it
would destroy. Its other decisions use Tactical v14. On the 64 previously
replay-verified current-core policy duels at
`.cache/goat-ai/fixed_policy_value_44000_44015/`, Heavy Storm was a legal
activation in 311 of 31,729 recorded decisions; the strict guard changed
Tactical's selected action in 48 decisions across 16 duels. This is an
offline disagreement count on policy-visited states, not a win-rate result.

In a predeclared head-to-head evaluation against unchanged Tactical v14, the
variant scored **119 wins, 119 losses, and 2 draws** over 240 terminal games:
all 15 pairings of six sourced tournament Main Decks, both deck assignments,
both seats, and seeds 55000–55003. Its score was **50.0%**, with a paired
bootstrap 95% interval of **48.75–51.25%**. First-seat score was 58.75%; the
second-seat score was 41.25%, illustrating the seat effect rather than a
guard advantage. There were 100,780 decisions, maximum 1,425 in one game.
The four-worker tournament took a measured 15.687 seconds on the logged
Linux x86_64 host. These sampled experimental-core games do not establish a
playing-strength gain or historical-ruling correctness. Keep the guard
opt-in and do not promote it as the demonstration teacher.

The evaluator initially mislabeled the named Tactical variant as teacher
version 1. Its report metadata now records both sides as base Tactical v14;
the variant name distinguishes the extra guard. Rerunning after that fix
produced exactly the same 240 game records. The corrected ignored report is
`.cache/goat-ai/card_advantage_vs_tactical_55000_55003_corrected.json`
(SHA-256 `5cc7f681af3e90ee307977925c3cae3711652de989ab055a92f90a579fd082da`).
It includes the source, native asset, script-tree, deck, and schedule hashes.
Reproduce from the pinned native setup with:

```bash

  .venv/bin/python scripts/evaluate_native.py \
  --native-root .cache/goat-ai --engine experimental \

```

## Synthetic maximum counter menu benchmark (27 October 2026)

`scripts/benchmark_counter_allocation.py` constructs a protocol-only
`MSG_SELECT_COUNTER` prompt with two visible cards, 32,767 counters on each,
and a cost of 32,767. The first staged decision has **32,768** legal amount
choices. This is the representable maximum for a single card in the current
signed 16-bit native response; it is not a witnessed GOAT duel state. A
width-32, feature-v28 PyTorch policy scored every choice with finite logits.

On Linux 6.8, an Intel Core i7-10700K, PyTorch 2.5.1+cpu, and one Torch
thread, three repeats gave median times of **0.019 s** to decode the native
prompt, **0.361 s** to build public actions, **0.807 s** to encode features,
and **0.038 s** for policy inference. Peak process RSS was **381.5 MiB**;
this includes the Python and PyTorch runtime and is not the incremental
memory attributable only to the counter decision. The ignored JSON report is
`.cache/goat-ai/counter_allocation_benchmark_20261027.json` (SHA-256
`7c5a6bd735b0d19d016bcfee8b87e760d5a9744413bcff7227d6c28f535c500b`).
Reproduce the same synthetic workload after installing the `ml` extra:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONPATH=src:. .venv/bin/python \
  scripts/benchmark_counter_allocation.py \
  --cards 2 --available 32767 --total 32767 --width 32 --repeats 3
```

The elapsed times will vary by machine. This measures the worst single-card
choice menu, not complete-duel speed or competitive strength. Multiple such
menus in parallel workers could create a material memory load; the project
has no observed native frequency estimate for this extreme prompt.

## Isolated native deck probe (28 October 2026)

The random-deck probe now has opt-in `--isolate-games`. Each seed runs in a
separate Python process. A native crash is recorded as a failed game with its
worker exit code and any generated decklist hashes, while later seeds still
run. Successful child reports contribute their replay, visibility, card-action,
and loaded-asset counts to one top-level report; each child report remains
under `OUTPUT/isolated/seed_N/report.json`. The output directory must be empty
before starting, which prevents a stale child report from being mistaken for
the current run. The CLI still exits nonzero if any game failed.

A regression simulates a worker exit of `-11` after writing both decklists,
checks their retained hashes, and confirms the next seed reaches terminal and
replay-verifies. A real four-seed tournament-card run on seeds 10800–10803
completed **4/4 terminal**, **3,330/3,330 replay-verified and visibility-audited
decisions**. Seed, deck hashes, decision count, terminal result, action kinds,
error, and verified-decision count match the corresponding four games from
the earlier single-process 40-seed sweep. The ignored combined report is
`.cache/goat-ai/tournament_mix_isolated_10800_10803/report.json` (SHA-256
`eb6cc6b0c6a4fd6a91f421a3d4d3eb79daa85e26b901682cf98de422fbb24f5b`).
Reproduce with the [tournament-card probe command above](#tournament-card-mix-protocol-sweep-28-october-2026),
using a fresh output directory, `--seed 10800 --seeds 4 --isolate-games`.
Process isolation makes failure triage possible; it does not repair a native
crash or certify historical card behavior.

## Independent frozen-opponent sampling stream (28 October 2026)

The self-play trainer now offers `--independent-opponent-rng`. Without it,
the sampled learner and frozen neural opponent share one Torch generator in a
duel, so an extra random draw by either player changes the other's future
action samples. The opt-in mode derives a separate deterministic opponent
stream from the duel seed. It applies to sequential, worker, and batched PPO
rollouts; the default shared stream is retained for reproduction of earlier
experiments. The checkpoint configuration and each replay record the flag.
This does not change the native duel seed or expose hidden state.

The local native rollout test passed for one worker, two workers, and batched
inference with a frozen snapshot opponent: reports, decision trajectories,
and updated model tensors matched exactly across all three paths. The full
`tests/test_parallel_rollout.py` file passed **8 tests** with two existing
TorchScript tracing warnings. A two-game restricted-engine CLI smoke run on
vanilla fixtures, seeds 90200–90201, produced two terminal games (one learner
win, one loss), **697 decisions**, and a checkpoint with the opt-in flag.
Both replay files passed exact native verification and the player-visibility
audit. The checkpoint SHA-256 is
`d0350547f30993cf920802d079675c188f9803bd9e4677e9516914587822e3ec`;
the replay SHA-256 values are
`1b4bc8daf4ff3035f40c307e6b77da9c6ec7174cf9ef3a644ea31c6b06f0f04b`
and `2e6c049dc0a0794135eb95ceebcd7f0f16069ce971bcc1719f5a98b373d781df`.

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONPATH=src:. .venv/bin/python scripts/train_self_play.py \
  .cache/goat-ai/fv23_current_tactical_broader_33000_33031.pt \
  --output .cache/goat-ai/independent_rng_smoke_90200.pt \
  --native-root .cache/goat-ai --engine restricted \
  --matchup examples/decks/vanilla_probe.ydk examples/decks/vanilla_reverse.ydk \
  --seed 90200 --games 2 --historical-probability 1 \
  --independent-opponent-rng --policy-update clipped_ppo \
  --ppo-rollout-games 2 --rollout-workers 2 --snapshot-every 2 \
  --ppo-epochs 1 --ppo-batch-size 16 --max-decisions 3000
```

This smoke run checks isolation and reproducibility of the sampling path. It
does not measure a competitive strength gain or close M4's self-play gate.

### Mixed-deck self-play with independent opponent sampling

Starting from the selected feature-v23 checkpoint, a clipped-PPO trial used
the new independent frozen-opponent stream on two sourced Main Deck pairings:
Jesse Twohig 2005 Goat Control versus Montague Warrior, and DingoSig Chaos
Return versus Weirdchamp Bazoo Return. A four-role schedule covered both
decks in both learner seats over seeds 90300–90363. It used 64 terminal
games, four-game frozen rollouts, four workers, two PPO epochs, batch 32,
per-episode weighting, a learner-deck baseline, parent KL weight 0.5,
learning rate 0.00005, and a 50% historical-snapshot probability with
Tactical-v14 otherwise. The realized training opponents were 33 Tactical
and 31 frozen snapshots. The sampled learner went 21–40–3 against this
mixture; this is a training outcome, not a strength estimate. The trainer
reported 19.22 seconds and 3,951 learner decisions. All 64 trajectories,
covering **24,851 decisions**, passed exact native replay verification and
the player-visibility audit. The checkpoint SHA-256 is
`06d3d8ec4d19de8935eace5d40ed586e5c7de57a022ccc1e045d20aa735af40b`;
the ignored replay-audit report SHA-256 is
`55320db450a41742d1044ebb559705427f19bd0dd6d3bd9c10c87188549639b8`.

Held-out evaluation used two other pairings: Roberto Martinez Phoenix
Control/Jae Kim Zombie and Rhymus Lizo Goat Control/WikiFormat Dimension
Fusion. Both deck assignments, both policy seats, and seeds 90400–90407
produced 64 direct child-versus-parent games. The evaluator rejected any
Main Deck composition used in either checkpoint's training. The child went

matched Tactical-v14 schedule, seeds 90408–90415, the child went **22–42**

points**. Neither comparison establishes a gain. The parent remains the

## Public face-up age v29 controlled pilot (28 October 2026)

Schema v26 makes each face-up field card's public age available to agents.
To check whether the new policy feature immediately helps, the selected v23
checkpoint recorded eight terminal games against Tactical-v14 on seeds
90500–90501. The two training pairings were Jesse Twohig 2005 Goat Control
versus Insids Chaos Control, and Cas Stomphorst Flip Control versus Daryl
Gessler Gravekeeper. Both policy seats were used. All **3,819 decisions**
passed exact native replay verification and the player-visibility audit.
Swords of Revealing Light was face-up in **540** decisions, including **220**
with multiple legal actions. Its public age was greater than zero in **185**
of those multi-option decisions. The ignored local manifest is
`.cache/goat-ai/public_age_policy_90500_90501/manifest.json` (SHA-256
`8d66cd8cecf47a9d619cc3b8eb21d809d81d2978353ff32773bd6cbd09add175`).

Two one-epoch clones used the same 710 multi-option Tactical-v14 synthetic
labels from those verified policy-visited states, the same v23 parent, width
32, seed 90500, batch 16, learning rate 0.00001, and batched forward with
forced choices omitted. The controlled v28 branch added counter-allocation
inputs; v29 added the public age input on top of v28. The new age input was
zero at warm start and had weight norm **0.000667** after fitting. Checkpoint
SHA-256 values are `d81936ca71316ca8a6b8a663e724c4c172d2640f0d3f8ebfe1bb730ee42b92d9`
for v28 and `70bf7e11defe308db2d5af61774f5a266686f73618e2096a31fe70aef9185d7b`
for v29. These labels are a heuristic's choices, not human expertise.

Held-out evaluation used Roberto Martinez Phoenix Control versus Jae Kim
Zombie and Rhymus Lizo Goat Control versus the WikiFormat Dimension Fusion
list. Both deck assignments and policy seats were tested on seeds
90600–90603, with the evaluator rejecting every Main Deck composition found
in either checkpoint's training provenance. Against the unchanged selected
v23 parent, **both v28 and v29 went 16–16** over 32 games, and all 32 paired
games had identical outcomes and decision counts. Direct v29-versus-v28 play
also split **16–16** over 32 games. At the 185 aged-Swords multi-option
training states, the two children chose the same greedy action in every case;
their maximum absolute action-logit difference was below **0.0001**. This
pilot does **not** show a competitive benefit from v29. The Tactical teacher
does not use the new age value, the sample is small, and the held-out matchup
has strong deck-assignment effects. Keep the selected v23 checkpoint.

To diagnose why the 240-game child above did not improve, the selected v23

the learner went 86–153–1 against 124 Tactical and 116 frozen-snapshot

decisions. All **124,104 decisions** in the 240 saved trajectories independently

`db82c6f8398de5f2d1b1164c765d664e04187be3b801d35448079a1406586af9`.

## Frozen visible-value local-advantage PPO ablation (28 October 2026)

An opt-in `--ppo-gae-lambda` now applies [generalized advantage estimation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02438)
to PPO's learner decisions using the existing frozen, player-visible resource
ridge. It uses undiscounted (`gamma=1`) transitions between successive
learner decisions and a terminal-only duel reward; opponent and forced moves
between those decisions are part of the transition. Lambda 1 is exactly the
existing terminal-return-minus-value advantage. The option requires a
verified frozen ridge and cannot be combined with leave-one-out return
baselines. Neither future outcomes nor hidden native state enter the value
prediction. This is an experimental credit-assignment signal, not a playing
strength claim.

A four-game native smoke run completed and all **1,846** decisions replay-
verified and passed the visibility audit. Two matched 240-duel continuations
then used the selected v23 parent, seeds 91000–91239, the same three training
pairings and PPO settings as the earlier 0.5-KL continuation, and the same
frozen ridge artifact
`.cache/goat-ai/frozen_resource_ridge_48300_48323.json` (SHA-256
`7115d29f4a6bedd2de870d26f43c570a902ab342a50593d185e4aa55dbb092dc`).
Only local-advantage lambda differed: the control used the existing
terminal-return-minus-value estimator, and the candidate used lambda **0.5**.
Both arms reached **240/240 terminal** with no decision cap. The control's
training record was **83–155–2**, 20,755 learner decisions, and **114.00 s**
reported wall time; the candidate's was **87–151–2**, 20,176 learner decisions,
and **109.98 s**. All **125,989 control** and **121,477 candidate** recorded
decisions independently replay-verified and passed the visibility audit. The
ignored checkpoints are `.cache/goat-ai/ppo_ridge_control_240_91000_91239.pt`
(SHA-256 `5156aa0a2ca5189e1c52d46865c1426f01c61f79ca2249a6d51e35ea933a62ee`)
and `.cache/goat-ai/ppo_ridge_gae05_240_91000_91239.pt` (SHA-256
`5ff7fe8704d8511de6f48ffc3d51b558312dafdfd26945f50b5d482cd5f98cc5`).
On eight verified parent-policy replays, the control matched **703/710**
multi-option greedy decisions and the candidate **704/710**. The agreement
report is `.cache/goat-ai/ppo_ridge_gae05_agreement_90500_90501.json`,
SHA-256 `b95f07715fb9874da1c014c62ea6a8d4c0c3b26b1a6e9d628bb485fc6173601a`.

Evaluation used Phoenix Control against WikiFormat Dimension Fusion with
both deck assignments and both policy seats. Both Main Deck compositions
were absent from the policy checkpoint training games and from all 96 ridge
training replays; the latter was checked by reading the artifact's hashed
replays and comparing Main Deck composition hashes. Phoenix Control appeared
in an earlier ridge transfer check, so this is a training-deck holdout but
not a completely untouched model-selection family. On fresh seeds
91700–91715, lambda-0.5 scored **28–35–1** directly against the return-based
control: **44.5% score**, paired 95% interval **36.7–52.3%**. On matched seeds
91716–91731 against Tactical-v14, lambda-0.5 scored **16–47–1**, the control
**21–42–1**, and the selected parent **17–46–1**. The strict report comparator
verified the same deck files, schedule, opponent, native assets, code, and
unseen policy Main Decks. Candidate-minus-control score was **−7.81
percentage points**, paired 95% interval **−15.63 to −1.56 points**. The
return-based control itself scored **31–32–1** directly against the selected
parent on fresh seeds 91732–91747, with a paired interval **38.3–59.4%**;
its matched Tactical difference from the parent was **+6.25 points**,
interval **−1.56 to +14.06 points**. Neither child is promoted. This
particular frozen-value GAE signal did not improve held-out play, and the
candidate changed only six greedy decisions on the fixed diagnostic sample.

The five ignored reports (candidate versus control, candidate versus Tactical,
control versus Tactical, parent versus Tactical, control versus parent) are

`.cache/goat-ai/ppo_ridge_gae05_vs_tactical_91716_91731.json`,

## Independent whitelist Fusion and Tactical protocol sweeps (28 October 2026)

SHA-256 `48763d36b1beba3ce37782d7d41cbee58fefe8f65573ab53090e319674bc5358`.

its seed without erasing later results. Both sweeps required terminal outcomes
below 3,000 decisions, independently replay-verified each saved trajectory,
and audited player-visible decisions and legal actions.

The broad whitelist run paired independently generated legal 40-card Main
Decks, each with 15 sampled Fusion cards. It forced three Scapegoats and
three Metamorphoses into each Main Deck and Thousand-Eyes Restrict into each
Extra Deck. On seeds **11300–11399**, **100/100** duels reached terminal;
all **108,360/108,360** decisions replay-verified and passed the visibility
audit. The audit counted 906 hidden-field, 6,619 opponent-field, and 81
opponent-hand legal choices. The run loaded **1,349** distinct native assets,
including **241** absent from the previous 40-seed Fusion-stress sweep; it
exercised **32** action kinds. Its ignored report is
`.cache/goat-ai/whitelist_fusion_stress_11300_11399/report.json` (SHA-256
`2324707f2e4139fd7c9823703a8347ed1fbef7ba1e17438ce77a7ed7dc21ebfe`).

those decisions again. The repeat report SHA-256 is
`128c56feed0301977d8b758854db4f2b65a4165ac32c552263e5cada2ef35305`.

The second sweep generated independent legal decks from the six sourced
tournament Main Decks and used Tactical-v14 for both seats. On seeds
**11400–11449**, **50/50** duels reached terminal; all **24,009/24,009**
decisions replay-verified and passed the visibility audit. It loaded 103
native assets and exercised 26 action kinds. It selected 86 distinct
responder/preceding-link card pairs, **62** of which were not selected in

(SHA-256 `40b2370ccabd0e2888ade90e04e6e87ad242682d2915de075908cf10f6b12f86`).

The native probe regression suite passed **9/9** with
`GOAT_AI_NATIVE_ROOT=.cache/goat-ai`. These results widen M1 protocol and

## Raw action-margin diagnostic for the 240-duel PPO child (28 October 2026)

The reusable `scripts/audit_policy_margins.py` replays each duel against the
pinned native engine, audits player-visible observations, rejects seeds used
to train either checkpoint, and measures the gap between the two highest raw
network logits at each multi-option demonstrator decision. This diagnostic
uses the eight previously inspected parent-policy/Tactical-v14 replays from
seeds 90500–90501. They are held out from both checkpoint training sets, but
they are **not** an untouched model-selection test set. The parent is the
selected feature-v23 checkpoint (SHA-256
`975d06284b3035bc8bf8dbafa041a8a25a80195574d1ff695f2fbd25d1c7ff45`);
the child is the 240-duel mixed-deck PPO continuation (SHA-256
`05698f306769dcb8cca873a048588010d5f74851a3f0137cfcc4acc7dcabc96c`).

All eight trajectories replay-verified and passed visibility audits. Of **710**
multi-option parent-policy decisions, the child changed **7** final choices.
The parent's raw top-two margin had median **2.817** overall; **448/710**
decisions had a margin of at least 2. Among the seven changed choices, its
median margin was **0.091** and maximum **0.191**. Among the 703 unchanged
choices, median margin was **2.840**. The child had median raw margin **2.773**.
This is consistent with the update moving near-tied decisions while leaving
larger existing preferences intact on this sample. It does not prove the
cause of the held-out competitive plateau: raw logits are not calibrated
probabilities, policy guards can alter final choices, and the sample has
already been used for other diagnostics. The next M4 experiment should
test an independently sourced decision signal or a targeted correction of
high-margin errors on *new* held-out deck families and seeds, with direct
competitive evaluation before promotion.

Reproduce with:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONPATH=src:. .venv/bin/python scripts/audit_policy_margins.py \
  --parent .cache/goat-ai/fv23_current_tactical_broader_33000_33031.pt \
  --child .cache/goat-ai/ppo_mixed_240_91000_91239.pt \
  --output .cache/goat-ai/ppo_mixed_240_margins_90500_90501.json \
  .cache/goat-ai/public_age_policy_90500_90501/matchup_*.json
```

The ignored JSON report has SHA-256
`33c2159c53a911bfdad8e062c4591168eae1d71dce56a80c92cacd336ddef951`;
it records the eight exact replay hashes and verified decision counts. The
diagnostic is off-policy and is not a tournament result.

### Legal-action representation collision audit (28 October 2026)

`scripts/audit_action_encoding.py` compares every action-specific tensor row
within each recorded legal set. It uses the checkpoint's pinned vocabulary and
player-visible trajectory observations; it does not infer playing strength.
For the eight replay-verified Seattle/Rhymus review trajectories, selected
feature v23 had 1,422 decisions with multiple actions and 9,280 legal actions.
Seven groups (272 actions) shared identical encodings. Three groups were
structurally identical choices, such as selecting a duplicate copy of the
same card. Four groups contained **distinct** choices: two `announce_card`
prompts and two `select_option` prompts. None of the 22 shortlisted
policy-versus-Tactical review pairs collide; their 737 within-prompt action
pairs are distinct.

Re-encoding the same visible records with experimental feature v30 leaves
five collision groups (268 actions) and only two distinct-choice groups,
both `announce_card`. Its option-ordinal feature separates the two option
prompts. In both card-announcement prompts, different card codes fall outside
the checkpoint vocabulary and map to the shared unknown-card index; the
other v23/v30 action features do not encode their identity. Preference labels
that distinguish those card names therefore cannot be fitted by either
version. This audit does not justify promoting v30 or claim a competitive gain.

Reproduce from the pinned environment:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src:. .venv/bin/python scripts/audit_action_encoding.py \
  .cache/goat-ai/fv23_current_tactical_broader_33000_33031.pt \
  .cache/goat-ai/seattle_parent_review_99200_99201/matchup_*_seed_*.json
```

Pass `--feature-version 30` to audit that alternative with the same
vocabulary. The ignored v23 and v30 report hashes are respectively
`4ca0b6eed16e7c6fb1c038f10742c8adfaa1c55305fd7908f11838aac150eb8c`
and `f0a628b1af6a3802344c8df522bf78ff8a2a69ecc74b80f30f64f360e356f026`.

An opt-in **feature v31** now appends 32 exact binary card-code inputs for
`announce_card`, plus a bit indicating that the announced name is in the
player-visible tracked opponent hand. The code must be a positive 32-bit
native card ID; other action kinds receive zeros. The v23-to-v31 loader
zero-extends the new action, counter, option, and public-card-age inputs, so
the selected parent remains unchanged at initialization. On all 22 current
review prompts, the warmed-up v31 model's maximum absolute logit difference
from v23 was **2.38×10⁻⁷**. The v31 encoding audit of the same eight
trajectories found **zero distinct-choice collision groups**; the remaining
three groups (eight actions) are structurally identical duplicate choices.
The ignored v31 audit report has SHA-256
`8fa5aa905a3aaa304ef563e5949c066347a366cb59ecbf62e947575a9a96c2e4`.
To reproduce, use the command above with `--feature-version 31`.

This establishes a learnable representation for card-announcement labels,
not that such labels exist or that v31 plays better. Feature v23 remains the
selected competitive checkpoint. V31 needs independent reviewed decisions,
training, and held-out competitive evaluation before promotion.

### First-offered activation probe (29 October 2026)

An opt-in `first_activation` agent now picks an offered `activate` or `chain`
action for a card ID it has not yet activated in that duel, using only the
acting player's legal actions. It falls back to seeded random play after
those first opportunities. This probes native decision and effect paths; it
is not a competitive agent or a historical-ruling oracle.

On the same seed-120000 partition of 1,624 canonical Main Deck IDs into 41
decks as the earlier random-agent suite, and with identical native assets and
deck bytes, all **21** first-activation duels reached terminal and all
**21,898** decisions replay-verified and passed visibility auditing. Distinct
effect activation IDs offered/selected rose from the random run's **308/281**
to **339/339**. Because choices change future states, the new run also missed
54 IDs selected by random play; the counts are coverage of visited paths,
not a strictly nested comparison.

A second independently shuffled partition at seed 120001 completed **21/21**
duels and verified **22,355** decisions. It offered **350** distinct activation
IDs and selected **347**. The two first-activation partitions selected **480**

Repeating seed 120001 with one worker rather than four gave identical ordered
decisions and winners in all 21 duels, with identical deck and native asset

still did not have their effects exercised and these runs do not prove
historical correctness.

## Resolved material changes for monster abilities and card effects (28 October 2026)

The experimental `scripts/audit_effect_material.py` reads only recorded
player-visible observations and selected legal actions. It counts hand cards
and controlled non-token field cards relative to the opponent before an
activation and at the first later decision after its chain resolves. Printed
card Type identifies monster abilities, including field and hand activations,
independently of the native action kind (`activate` or `chain`). It also covers
Spell/Trap effects. Tokens are excluded using their printed Token type, and
unknown face-down opponent identities remain unknown. Every input duel is
exactly replay-verified and visibility-audited first.

The current count is
`(own hand size + own non-token field cards) − (opponent hand size + opponent non-token field cards)`.
The reported `material_delta` is that margin **after chain closure minus before
activation**. Both face-up and face-down controlled cards count as one, even
when their identity is hidden from the acting player. For example, Pot of
Greed activated from the hand and resolving without another effect changes
the margin by +1: one card is spent and two are drawn. Raigeki Break activated
from a Set field card, discarding one own hand card and destroying one
opposing field card, changes it by −1. A monster ability that removes one
opposing field card without spending another card changes it by +1. These are
observed board-and-hand counts, not automatic judgments of play quality.

On the already recorded 64 current-core self-play duels from seeds
97000–97063, all **27,511 decisions** passed those checks. The diagnostic
found **228 selected monster-ability activations** and **849 selected
Spell/Trap activations**. A stable decision after chain closure existed in
the same turn for **226** and **839**, respectively. The remaining 12
activations ended without that decision boundary, usually at terminal Ring
of Destruction resolution; they were not assigned a material delta. Among
the measured monster abilities, 78 chains had a negative, 55 a zero, and 93
a positive material change. For Spell/Trap effects the counts were 266, 374,
and 199. Another selected activation occurred before closure in 9 monster
and 109 Spell/Trap chains, so those deltas combine multiple selected effects.
Automatic triggers can also contribute even when that count is zero.

One measured example is Black Luster Soldier's field ability in seed 97002
at decision 554. The next target choice selects its controller's own monster,
and the observed chain loses one net non-token card. This demonstrates that
the new diagnostic includes ability activations; it does **not** establish
that every negative delta is a bad play. It omits Life Points, Graveyard
utility, card quality, tempo, delayed effects, future draws, and hidden
opponent cards. Responses and automatic triggers confound causal attribution.
It reports the result of the **selected** line, not the expected result of
every alternative legal action. No automated training labels or policy change
were made from these numbers.

The ignored report is
`.cache/goat-ai/effect_material_human14_97000_97063.json` (SHA-256
`8cf5f7d9aba42eb18db05a188d2930402167327bc61f7e8042e157050a5e6ea7`).
Reproduce it after native setup with:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONPATH=src:. .venv/bin/python \
  scripts/audit_effect_material.py \
  .cache/goat-ai/human14_ppo_mixed_64_97000_97063_replays/episode_*.json \
  --native-root .cache/goat-ai \
  --output .cache/goat-ai/effect_material_human14_97000_97063.json
```

The next training experiment can use this observed signal as a small
auxiliary value target or carefully constructed reward potential, then
compare it with the unchanged policy on held-out Main Decks and seeds.

### Does immediate material change track the duel winner?

The same 64 verified duels were re-audited with a paired outcome check. For
each source type, it compares the winner's and loser's **mean observed material
change within the same duel**. A duel enters the comparison only when both
seats had at least one resolved activation of that type, with no additional
selected activation before the chain closed. The 95% intervals resample
whole duels 10,000 times with seed 0; they do not treat every activation as
an independent game.

| Source | Paired duels | Winner minus loser, cards | Bootstrap 95% interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Monster ability | 30 | +0.066 | −0.307 to +0.449 |
| Spell/Trap effect | 63 | +0.129 | −0.035 to +0.304 |

Both intervals include zero. The winner was only slightly ahead on this
metric, with no clear association in this small sample. Moreover, winning
position, deck choice, timing, and opponent responses can affect both the
activation and the duel outcome. These numbers do not justify rewarding every
positive material delta or penalizing every negative one in PPO. Keep duel
outcome as the training objective; any auxiliary material signal needs a
separate controlled ablation on held-out decks and seeds.

The ignored schema-v2 report is
`.cache/goat-ai/effect_material_human14_97000_97063_v2.json` (SHA-256
`1aada6a08092d422c83d3ea77b6cc1001a5f3a33f5ac7ea6954771d1c78de1c5`).
It contains the same per-effect records as the schema-v1 report above; the
new field is `paired_outcome_association`. Reproduce it with the same command
above and a `_v2.json` output filename.

### Action-level material comparisons (29 October 2026)

The weak winner-level association above cannot decide whether an obviously
bad **choice at one prompt** should be discouraged. The `visible_material_choices_v4`
automated preference rule now keeps v3's own-only Nobleman and negative visible
Heavy Storm comparisons and adds two post-activation comparisons:

- For GOAT Black Luster Soldier and Chaos Sorcerer, it ranks an offered opposing
  monster target above banishing the actor's own, self-owned boss. It skips a
  borrowed boss, whose removal can have a different value when control ends.
- For Tribe-Infecting Virus, it uses only face-up monsters' current public
  Types to rank an offered Type with a better immediate opponent-minus-own
  destruction count above a Type that hits friendly monsters but no opposing
  ones. Face-down opponent Types are not read.

These are **synthetic pairwise hypotheses**, not expert labels or an assertion
that the activation was worthwhile. At a target/Type prompt, any activation
cost is already paid; comparing the remaining choices is narrower than
calling every negative resolved material change a bad move. The rule
recomputes during label validation, uses only the acting player's observation
and legal actions, and requires native replay and visibility verification.

Current-core collections at seeds 97000–97063 and 99000–99063 supplied
**76** and **59** comparisons from 26 and 27 replays. The first contained 30
own-only Nobleman, 19 negative Heavy Storm, 19 boss-target, and eight Tribe
comparisons. The second contained 16, 24, 18, and one respectively. Of the
combined 135 comparisons, **31** had the recorded choice on the disfavored
side; three of those were target/Type choices in the second collection. The

comparisons but, for own-only Nobleman and negative visible Heavy Storm,

### Reviewed own-card MST chain decision (29 October 2026)

Three newly saved local review choices from the seed-104400–104407 one-shot
queue passed queue-membership, legal-action, complete native replay, and
visibility validation. Two retained the recorded MST target **after** MST had
already been activated; these are conditional target approvals, not approval
of the earlier activation. One changed the earlier decision at zero-based
decision 301 of `ring_guard_blind_104400_104407/matchup_01_seed_104405_seat_1.json`:
chain a Set Mystical Space Typhoon while the player's own Mirror Force is
active, or Pass. The reviewer selected Pass. The validated preference file
SHA-256 is `700589b6aa98ab44762bbc8b3f7e7abad3f9c4b59d32646e8ccd0098fa7f7af9`.
The original selected feature-v23 checkpoint ranked MST first; its Pass-minus-
MST logit margin was **−3.774** at this replay-verified state. Neither the
exact replay nor its seed was used in that checkpoint's training metadata.

An offline exact-state branch used the recorded activation versus Pass with
the same frozen checkpoint and `greedy_own_loss_guard_v1` continuations. Both
branches ended in a loss for the reviewed player; they ran for 630 and 1,010
decisions respectively. All decisions in both trajectories replay-verified
and passed the visibility audit. The ignored branch report is
`.cache/goat-ai/one_shot_review_branch_104405_d301/report.json`. This one
branch establishes neither the reviewer's reason nor a competitive benefit
from changing the action. It does establish an actionable disagreement with
the selected model. The reviewed preference is preserved locally for later
training, but one changed label is insufficient to promote a new policy.

An opt-in `own_loss_guard_version=6` adds a narrower response check: when
the only destroyable back-row card is the player's own already resolving
one-shot Spell/Trap, defer MST if Pass is available. It excludes MST's own
Set slot, preserves MST if another field Spell/Trap exists, and consults only
public chain and field information plus printed card type. The exact reviewed
state changes from MST under v5 to Pass under v6. This is a strategic
preference and does not change legal actions or claim MST negates effects.

A fresh direct comparison on seeds 122000–122007 used the unchanged selected
v23 checkpoint on both sides, v6 versus v5, Phoenix Control against two
unseen Dimension Fusion Main Decks, both deck assignments and both seats.
All 64 games finished within the 3,000-decision cap; v6 scored **31–31–2**
against v5. The ignored report is
`.cache/goat-ai/own_loss_v6_vs_v5_122000_122007.json` (SHA-256
`12b966dbe691843bf08d2c0c88a2b3411b5c25850e3ff759566d192f44451faa`).
This test shows no gain and does not measure how often the new condition was
reached. The selected checkpoint and inference mode remain unchanged.

### Visible own-card loss opportunities in the guarded v23 corpus (29 October 2026)

The replay auditor now flags MST **at the activation prompt** when its only
field target is the acting player's already resolving one-shot Spell/Trap.
The corresponding opportunity count includes opponent-turn response windows,
and deduplicates repeated priority prompts by category, turn, and phase. The
check uses only the actor's observation and printed type of the public chain
source. A forced MST target prompt is not counted as another activation
choice. This audit definition is shared with experimental guard v6.

All 128 recorded `ring_guard_blind_104400_104407` v23/v1-guarded duels
replayed against the pinned native engine, passed the visibility audit, and
reproduced **37,132** greedy policy choices, of which **12,707** offered
multiple actions. The auditor found **18** conservative own-card-loss flags:
14 idle own-only Ring activations, two negative visible Heavy Storm trades,
one MST chained to its own one-shot card, and one own Ring target despite a
safe opposing target. It counted **22** distinct idle own-only Ring
opportunities and **3** own-one-shot MST response opportunities; the policy
selected the flagged action in **14/22** and **1/3**, respectively. The MST
case is viewer frame 302 of the reviewed seed-104405 replay. Other measured
upstream categories in this corpus had zero flagged choices: own-only
Nobleman **0/158**, own-only Heavy Storm **0/96**, idle own-back-row MST
**0/26**, Breaker with only friendly back row **0/18**, and owned Chaos boss
with no enemy monster **0/15**. There was no idle own-only Raigeki Break
opportunity under this definition. These are rates **per observed
opportunity**, not rates over all games or proof of optimal play. The v1
guard already suppresses several categories, so the zeros do not describe
an unguarded neural policy. The ignored report is
`.cache/goat-ai/ring_guard_blind_104400_104407/own_loss_opportunity_audit_v6.json`
(SHA-256 `deceb55ffbe39347ed0047012364ca063312113e10a6f5ad5cffaf7534ccac1d`).
The Ring concentration makes Ring timing and targets a higher-priority
review/training topic than the single MST example. These fixed replay states
do not establish a policy strength gain or justify promoting guard v6.

The review audit now distinguishes the narrower
`ring_visible_self_lethal_if_resolved` case from the 14 broad idle-own-Ring
flags. It requires every visible own face-up target to have ATK at least the
acting player's LP but below the opponent's LP, with no opposing face-up
monster. The check does not inspect hidden responses and therefore states
what the current visible damage would do **if Ring resolves unmodified**.
Exactly one of the 14 recorded activations meets this condition: seed 104401,
policy seat 0, viewer frame 746. The policy had 200 LP, the opponent 3,000 LP,
and targeted its own 300-ATK Sinister Serpent. The recorded native duel ended
four decisions later with the policy losing when Ring resolved. An exact-state
branch that instead chose End Phase also ultimately lost, after 775 decisions
rather than 749; both complete branches replay-verified and passed visibility
audit. The ignored branch report is
`.cache/goat-ai/ring_self_lethal_104401_d745/report.json`. This is a strong
negative example for **that activation's immediate consequence**, but it is
one state and does not prove that End Phase was the best move or that a new
neural policy is stronger.

## Batched parent-KL scoring pilot (29 October 2026)

The opt-in `--batched-forward --batch-size 16` path now scores the full
labeled set in padded, variable-action chunks during each parent-KL step and
batches its sampled preservation states. It uses the same weighted
cross-entropy and parent-KL objective and still performs one optimizer update
per step. Scalar behavior remains the default; the batched path requires a
supported feature-v10+ policy. A regression test compares the two paths on
mixed legal-action counts and nonuniform label weights.

The [Rhymus/Beastdown Tactical pilot](#rhymus-and-beastdown-on-policy-tactical-pilot-29-october-2026)
was rerun with identical four verified training duels, four current-core
preservation duels, 244 labels, 64 sampled preservation states, 120 steps,
seed 128016, learning rate 0.0001, and parent-KL weight 1. On this Linux
x86-64 host with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, scalar fit time was **86.66 seconds**;
batched fit time was **14.65 seconds** (**5.91×** faster). Total run wall time,
including replay verification and loading, fell from **90.47** to **18.35
seconds** (**4.93×** faster). The scalar and batched final labeled losses
were **0.271107** and **0.271116**; final sampled preservation KL values
were **0.0187027** and **0.0187035**. These small numerical differences are
expected from different floating-point reduction order.

On two separate native-replay-verified Seattle parent-policy trajectories,
the scalar and batched children selected the **same action at all 171
multi-option decisions**. These Seattle states contributed to the parent-KL
preservation pool, so this checks implementation agreement, not independent
playing strength. The ignored batched checkpoint and agreement report are
`.cache/goat-ai/fv23_rhymus_beast_tactical_kl120_batched_128016.pt` (SHA-256
`616b3a0a9f9f0af2926f10daa1de523fe6475dacc51e210a3a886c7bdc1819c1`)
and `.cache/goat-ai/rhymus_scalar_batched_agreement_99200.json` (SHA-256
`6b8dd270390c9f06fb99788f178fbe038fb474e762006dcb9942b79fbe594621`).
The batched child is not promoted; the previous held-out outcome test found
no convincing gain for this training signal.

Reproduce the scalar fit with the command in the Rhymus pilot above, then
repeat it with `--batched-forward --batch-size 16` and a different ignored
output path. Use `scripts/audit_policy_agreement.py --engine experimental
--checkpoint` for both children on the two
`seattle_parent_review_99200_99201/matchup_01_seed_99201_seat_{0,1}.json`
trajectories. The `--batch-size` flag controls scoring chunk size for
parent-KL; all labels still contribute to each update.

## Fixed-state branch diagnostics for two review flags (30 October 2026)

`scripts/evaluate_decision_branches.py` now reports the observed, player-visible
non-token hand-plus-field material margin through chain closure when the
selected branch action activates a card or effect. This is a realized material
change, not a prediction of strategic value; phase and Set branches report
`null` because they do not start an activation. The existing open-chain
diagnostic remains separate. Both diagnostics include the terminal
player-visible snapshot when a chain ends the duel; that snapshot is indexed
after the final decision in the report. The pinned native engine can retain
the last public chain link in a lethal terminal snapshot. A seeded pre-errata
Ring of Destruction fixture confirms that its final chain action is now
measured at the terminal snapshot: visible material margin changes from +1 to
0 while the opponent's Life Points fall to zero. This is a diagnostic of the
completed trajectory, not an inferred value for Ring in other positions.

For the replay-verified weak-sourced review, the recorded Heavy Storm at
decision 785 in `matchup_00_seed_132001_seat_1.json` lost one visible material
unit through resolution. Set, Battle Phase, and End Phase alternatives all
lost the same fixed-deal duel as the recorded activation. The recorded Breaker
activation at decision 271 in `matchup_00_seed_132000_seat_0.json` also lost
one visible material unit; Battle Phase and End Phase alternatives all won the
same fixed-deal duel. Reports live in the ignored review directory as
`branch_storm/report.json` (SHA-256
`4f7beeb878d1f3430383b98e0652073708a7c444752b2baac805eb0419a4d9fa`)
and `branch_breaker/report.json` (SHA-256
`1e8d464c2e2416c835140e0782b9e7d7f68cfc08fed77309c279ac66464cdc41`).
The updated activation-field reports for the recorded and Battle Phase
branches are `branch_storm_material/report.json` (SHA-256
`e508ff850f56d7baf7efff2911c8349e3db961acba76d577af176ccda206a431`)
and `branch_breaker_material/report.json` (SHA-256
`cefdac1b04a137038a1dd283b01e1c6d638f1cade5e6a97e0507bbd29555e35f`).
All branches reconstructed the source decision, completed, replay-verified,
and passed the visibility audit. A single fixed hidden deal and continuation
cannot label the best action or establish a strength gain; the diagnostic
helps identify activations for further human review and multi-deal evaluation.

selected v23 teacher corpus had 19 two-copy and six zero-copy Thunder search
labels at observed prompts, so both training-label quality and preference
preservation need attention before another large run. The teacher-label audit
hash is `887039d712373fabba87e81e9eb66dd36e890d5a1e78e4e52fb35a2674f73e0c`.

## Weighted PPO advantage normalization pilot (30 October 2026)

An opt-in `--ppo-normalize-advantages` centers and scales frozen-rollout
advantages using the same per-decision or per-episode weights as the PPO
update. A constant-advantage rollout keeps its original signal. The default
update remains unchanged. This is a training ablation, not a tactical rule.

Starting from selected feature-v23, the normalized and control arms each
played 32 games with eight rollout workers, two sourced pairings (Lolmarcus
Goat Control/Riclar Chaos Turbo and Montague Warrior/Ciriano Beastdown),
four-role scheduling, seeds 152100–152131, 16-game frozen PPO batches,
two epochs, minibatch 32, parent KL 0.5, and a 3,000-decision cap. Both
recorded 14 wins and 18 losses during self-play. The normalized arm recorded
3,210 learner decisions versus 3,200 for the control; all first 16 trajectory
JSON files matched byte-for-byte, before their first updates diverged. The
normalized arm's 32 complete trajectories and 19,430 decisions independently
replay-verified and passed the visibility audit. Its checkpoint SHA-256 is
`05636c36f89c78fba421a77af7764eda8bd6e0e8dd19925a85d30eefde9f6808`;
the unnormalized control is the 8-worker arm in the [memory benchmark](benchmarks.md#ppo-process-tree-memory-on-the-same-mixed-decks-2026-10-30).

On four previously unseen tournament Main Decks (Bryan Chaos, Rhymus Goat
Control, Mary Warrior, and Jae Zombie), both Deck assignments and seats,
seeds 152500–152507, the normalized child scored **35–29** directly against
the control over 64 games (paired 95% score interval 50.00–59.38%). On fresh
seeds 152600–152607 both children scored **30–34** against the selected v23
parent, with the same per-deck win counts. On matched Tactical-v14 seeds
152700–152707, normalization scored **27–37** versus the control's **25–39**;
the verified paired difference was +3.13 percentage points, 95% interval
0.00–7.81 points. Both extra wins were on Mary Warrior; the other three deck
assignments had identical scores. The candidate therefore has no demonstrated
gain over the selected parent and no broad transfer across these deck
families. Keep normalization opt-in and v23 selected.

baseline, per-episode weighting, parent KL 0.05, and a 3,000-decision cap.

the v23 arm recorded 26,592 decisions, 17 learner wins, 29 losses, and two
draws in 23.66 seconds; v32 recorded 26,562 decisions, 19 wins, 27 losses,

## Unfinished human-duel prefix pilot — 30 October 2026

The new journal importer replays every saved action on the pinned native core,

decisions in five unfinished browser games; a sixth had none. The trainer
froze the five source journals under private SHA-256-named snapshots in
ignored `.cache/goat-ai/human_journal_snapshots/`. No outcome was assigned to
any prefix, and the checkpoint marks each game as partial. These sources are
the player's own local recordings; none is committed or redistributed.

An exploratory one-epoch behavioral-cloning update started from the selected
feature-v23 checkpoint, used all 41 decisions with width 32, batch size 8,
learning rate 0.0001, seed 30990, and a batched forward pass. Verification
took **0.95 s**, fitting **0.57 s**, and training-choice greedy agreement moved
from **20/41** for the parent to **21/41** for the child; only **2/41** greedy
actions changed. Agreement on the fitted choices is not held-out skill.

The child played the selected parent directly with the same v1 visible
own-loss guard on both sides. Max Suffridge's 2005 Goat Control and Jae Kim's

scored **16–16** in 32 complete native duels. The 95% Wilson interval for its
decisive win rate is **33.63–66.37%**. The small prefix signal neither shows a
competitive gain nor justifies promoting the child; the selected v23 policy
remains unchanged. This pilot also does not validate the human quality of all

## Fresh random whitelist/Fusion protocol sample — 30 October 2026

Twenty independently seeded legal Main Decks, each against a distinct legal

165000–165019. Both seats used RandomAgent. Each Deck included a random legal
15-card Fusion Extra Deck and three Scapegoat/Metamorphosis copies to exercise
the Fusion route. Games ran in isolated workers with a 3,000-decision cap.
All **20/20** reached terminal without a reported error; complete replay
verification and player-visible audits covered **20,315** decisions. The
same seeds reproduced all 20 decision streams, terminal states, and outcomes.
Observed game lengths ranged from 172 to 1,630 decisions, mean 1,015.75.

were absent from the selected-activation sets of the three prior first-
activation whitelist partitions: Spiritualism, Burning Spear, Dragonic Attack,
Wave-Motion Cannon, Timidity, Metamorphosis, Remove Trap, Sword of Dragon's
Soul, Buster Rancher, GOAT Limiter Removal, and GOAT Thousand-Eyes Restrict.
These IDs extend sampled protocol coverage; some already have individual
historical fixtures. The duels do not certify the rulings of those cards or
arbitrary legal Decks.

(SHA-256 `5f5fd7e954a07a5136df8b62118f11c5e04a05bae73346c7564b47c47c58e5da`).
These are synthetic teacher demonstrations, not human play.

An initial parent-KL fit attempt correctly rejected six old parent-source
preservation trajectories because their recorded core/script hashes differ
from the current pinned assets. Fresh policy-versus-Tactical preservation
games were therefore collected on the current assets: four Goat Control/
Chaos Turbo games at seeds 168300–168301 and four Warrior/Bazoo Return games
at seeds 168400–168401. The exact selected-v23 checkpoint generated the
policy actions. All **8/8** games and 5,283 decisions replay-verified; the

`fv23_preserve_168400_b/`, SHA-256
`e8aad42418db5765a7bb400494e52fd9fd7f86161d2f89ee6742acbe85ae1f07`
and `4417c7e1d66410cf6bf60bdadd49a151abb2571f15f282b42bf7782520d32426`.
The trainer's explicit matching-parent preservation gate accepted these
trajectories, sampled 128 multi-option visible states, and fit a feature-v23,
width-32 child for 25 batched parent-KL steps at learning rate 0.0001 and KL
weight 0.5. The child checkpoint is ignored at
`.cache/goat-ai/fv23_crossdeck_tactical_168200.pt`, SHA-256

On fresh seeds 169000–169007 with the four untouched Beastdown, Chaos,
Phoenix Control, and Warrior Main Decks from the previous section, both deck
assignments and both policy seats were evaluated against Tactical-v14. The
child scored **22–41–1** and selected v23 scored **24–39–1** on the same 64-game
schedule. The checked paired score difference was **−3.13 percentage points**
(95% interval **−10.94 to +4.69**). Directly against the parent on the same

keep the original v23 selected. The parent varied from 11–53 on seeds
167000–167007 to 24–39–1 on 169000–169007, so comparisons across different
seed blocks must not be mistaken for a training effect. The evaluator did not
independently replay-verify each tournament game.

An opt-in `--verify-replays` mode was then added to the policy evaluator. It
reconstructs each terminal game from its selected actions and audits every
player-visible decision, in either serial or parallel workers. Repeating both

## Larger-step PPO transfer to four New Jersey decks (30 October 2026)

The earlier 240-game PPO child (`ppo_lr5e4_240_131000_131239.pt`) was tested
on the same four untouched New Jersey 2005 Main Decks and seeds 169000–169007
used for the selected v23 parent in the verified cross-deck Tactical comparison
above. Neither checkpoint trained on these exact Main Deck compositions or
YDK files. Both Deck assignments and both policy seats produced 64 games per
checkpoint against Tactical-v14, with no optional guard on either policy.
The child scored **17–46–1** (27.34% points); the parent scored **24–39–1**
(38.28% points). The strict matched-report comparator measured a child-minus-
parent difference of **−10.94 percentage points**, paired 95% bootstrap
interval **−18.75 to −1.56**. Child Deck scores were Beastdown 9–7, Chaos
2–14, Phoenix Control 2–14, and Warrior 4–11–1. The child worsened both
Beastdown and Warrior relative to the parent; its Phoenix score remained poor.

All **64/64** child duels, covering **37,581 decisions**, independently
replay-verified and passed the player-visibility audit. The parent report had
already verified 64/64 games and 37,024 decisions. The reports share pinned
core/card-script and source-code hashes, and the comparator checked the exact
deck files and unseen Main Deck compositions. The child report is
`.cache/goat-ai/ppo_lr5e4_vs_tactical_nj_169000_verified.json` (SHA-256
`003f2e1a964ce017161184bb05380c1dc8313e5fffa8ccaf9d6bb36984dfd725`);
the comparison is
`.cache/goat-ai/ppo_lr5e4_vs_parent_nj_169000_comparison.json` (SHA-256
`0a157828ae941b8a225d17a918203eb2997d1b2c93582423bd6e68edb12ac974`).
Reproduce with `scripts/evaluate_policy.py --engine experimental --opponent
tactical --both-deck-assignments --seed 169000 --seeds 8 --max-decisions 3000
--workers 4 --require-unseen-main-decks --reject-training-deck-hashes
--verify-replays` on the two named New Jersey pairings above, then compare to
`crossdeck_parent_vs_tactical_169000_verified.json` with
`scripts/compare_tournament_reports.py --verify-local-decks
--require-unseen-main-decks`.

This independently sourced transfer check contradicts promotion of the PPO
child despite its earlier gains on other decks. Keep the selected v23 parent;
M4 still needs a learned policy with reliable cross-deck strength.

## Guarded v23 on New Jersey 2005 holdout (30 October 2026)

Two replay-verified, unguarded v23/Tactical-v14 duels on Roberto Martinez's
Phoenix Control versus Mary Triatafilidi's Warrior list were recorded at
seeds 172000–172001 with the policy in the Phoenix seat. The policy lost both.
At decision 16 in seed 172000 it Set Magician of Faith, then activated
Nobleman of Crossout targeting that own Set monster while the opponent had no
Set monster. The existing policy replay auditor flagged this as its sole
visible own-card-loss instance among 407 policy decisions in those two duels.
This is a concrete example of a failure already covered by the optional
visible own-loss guard; the two-game sample cannot estimate its frequency.
The ignored collector manifest is
`.cache/goat-ai/phoenix_policy_audit_172000/manifest.json`; all four
seat-swapped collection duels (1,951 decisions total) replay-verified. The
policy-seat Phoenix audit is in the same folder as `audit.json`.

To measure the guarded inference mode on a broader schedule, the selected
feature-v23 checkpoint was rerun against Tactical-v14 on the exact four New
Jersey Main Decks and seeds 169000–169007 used for the verified unguarded
parent report above. Both Deck assignments and both policy seats were covered.
The guarded policy scored **33–31**, versus **24–39–1** unguarded, across
64 games each. The strict matched comparator measured a **+13.28 percentage
point** score difference (paired 95% interval **+5.47 to +21.88**). Guarded
Deck scores were Beastdown 13–3, Chaos 4–12, Phoenix Control 4–12, and
Warrior 12–4; Phoenix remains a weak assignment despite improving from 3–13.
All **64/64** guarded games and **37,201 decisions** independently
replay-verified and passed the player-visibility audit; the unguarded control
had previously verified 64 games and 37,024 decisions. The reports share the
same checkpoint, native assets, card scripts, source code, decks, and seeds.

The ignored guarded report is
`.cache/goat-ai/fv23_own_loss_guard_nj_169000_verified.json` (SHA-256
`114696750c0caa5484ba59a9deaf84e2eb283d03d65c06715fe34a8c00ca82ba`);
the comparison is
`.cache/goat-ai/fv23_guard_vs_plain_nj_169000_comparison.json` (SHA-256
`2d8e7d0b61e71f9ca0adae89f5be9c51bd0f5982dfe30c2890998567a14e6255`).
Reproduce with `scripts/evaluate_policy.py --engine experimental --opponent
tactical --own-loss-guard --both-deck-assignments --seed 169000 --seeds 8
--max-decisions 3000 --workers 4 --require-unseen-main-decks
--reject-training-deck-hashes --verify-replays` on the same two New Jersey

`scripts/compare_tournament_reports.py --verify-local-decks

The browser game and local EDOPro policy room already use this guarded mode.
This is measured inference-time error prevention, not a learned improvement
to the neural checkpoint. M4 still requires stronger unguarded cross-deck
learning and independent human-quality evidence.

## Guarded PPO collection pilot (30 October 2026)

The self-play trainer now has `--learner-own-loss-guard` for clipped PPO. It
applies the deployed visible own-loss guard v1 both when sampling learner
actions and when computing old and updated action probabilities. Trajectories
still record every legal action and identify the guard version. The mode is
opt-in; loading its checkpoint does not automatically enable the guard for
inference.

Starting from the selected v23 checkpoint, a four-game pilot used Roberto
Martinez's Phoenix Control against the Warrior probe, both learner seats,
seeds 174000–174003, Tactical-v14 opponents, two CPU rollout workers, one
PPO epoch, and a 5e-5 learning rate. All four games terminated and their
trajectories independently replay-verified and passed the player-visibility
audit. The learner made 275 multi-option decisions; the guard excluded at
least one option at 17 of those decisions, with zero excluded actions chosen.
The learner won one game and lost three. Runtime reported by the trainer was
4.17 seconds on this local run. These four games establish that the guarded
rollout and update paths execute; they cannot measure a strength change.
The ignored pilot checkpoint is
`.cache/goat-ai/guarded_ppo_pilot_174000_174003.pt` (SHA-256
`b2ed7954e298f4258d3c99754905e3342153f42d23ae383cdd2c13491286abde`).
Its four replay files are beside it in
`guarded_ppo_pilot_174000_174003_replays/`.

Reproduce by running `python -m scripts.train_self_play` with the selected
v23 checkpoint, `--engine experimental`, the two named Main Decks,
`--seed 174000 --games 4 --policy-update clipped_ppo
--learner-own-loss-guard --baseline-opponent tactical
--historical-probability 0 --ppo-rollout-games 2 --rollout-workers 2
--ppo-epochs 1 --ppo-batch-size 16 --snapshot-every 2
--learning-rate 5e-5 --max-decisions 3000` and an unused output path.
The next gate is a larger, balanced, held-out comparison against both the
unguarded parent and Tactical on unrelated deck families, with the guard
disabled at evaluation time to test learned improvement.
